summary_paragraph: A woman with history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass status post reversal complicated by chronic abdominal pain, prior ulcers, suspected bacterial overgrowth, and dependence on gastrostomy tube feeds presented with acute-on-chronic burning epigastric pain and nausea with one episode of non-bloody, non-bilious emesis. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, normal laboratory testing without electrolyte abnormalities, and imaging (CXR and abdominal radiographs) without pneumoperitoneum or bowel obstruction. She was managed medically with pain and nausea control, continued tube feeds at goal, initial NPO status with gradual advancement to clear and then full liquids as tolerated, and optimization of reflux/dysmotility/overgrowth therapy including a trial of erythromycin, addition of nightly ranitidine, and discharge with rifaximin; H. pylori serology was sent and remained pending at discharge. Symptoms stabilized without further emesis, and she was discharged home ambulatory with close bariatric surgery follow-up and guidance to continue tube feeds and slowly advance oral intake over weeks to months as tolerated.
